results.title: EC tells Supreme Court Centre’s citizenship scrutiny powers are limited - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: constitutional_authority: Election Commission clarifies citizenship scrutiny powers

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: Election Commission of India dismissed arguments by opposition parties regarding the Centre's exclusive authority to scrutinise citizenship, asserting its own jurisdiction.
notes.fact_box: The Election Commission of India argued that its power to scrutinise citizenship is limited to determining when or how an Indian citizen acquired foreign citizenship. This is based on Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955. The EC also asserted its authority under Article 324 and 326 of the Constitution.

prelims_pointers.text: Article 324 empowers the Election Commission to supervise and control the conduct of elections.
Article 326 stipulates that Indian citizenship is a constitutional precondition for entry into the voter list.
Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, vests the Centre with the authority to determine when or how an Indian citizen acquired foreign citizenship.

notes.mains_question: Examine the jurisdiction of the Election Commission in scrutinising citizenship and its alignment with constitutional provisions.
